_comment: Per-source stale-threshold hours for the source-health alert engine (src/api/source_health_alerts.py). The 2h scheduled-refresh cron (.github/workflows/scheduled-refresh.yml) writes every source's CSV unconditionally on a successful fetch, so CSV mtime tracks 'fetch succeeded' rather than 'vendor published new content'. A 24h threshold therefore catches ~12+ consecutive fetch failures and is the policy: the operator wants to know about scrape outages within a day, not weeks. A source is matched by full registry key (e.g. ``flockFantasySf``) OR by vendor prefix (e.g. ``fantasyPros`` covers ``fantasyProsSf`` + ``fantasyProsIdp`` + ``fantasyProsFitzmaurice``). Default (for any source not listed): 24 hours.
_comment_soft: Sources listed in 'soft' are still reported everywhere (on-site stale banner, email alerts with their existing cooldown, the freshness-watchdog summary) but do NOT hard-fail the scheduled-refresh workflow for the first 'softEscalateHours'. Use this only for sources whose staleness recurs for reasons outside the cron's control. idpShow authenticates with a browser-minted cookie (deploy/idpshow_fetch_and_push.sh) that the operator must periodically re-mint by hand; when it lapses, one expiring cookie should not turn every 2h run red. SOFT IS A DELAY, NOT AN EXEMPTION: past softEscalateHours a soft source hard-fails like any other. Before 2026-07-27 the flag had no upper bound, which quietly meant 'this source is unmonitored' — a lapsed cookie and a dead vendor looked identical forever. Matched by exact key or vendor prefix, same as thresholds. (draftSharks was temporarily soft-flagged 2026-07-25 while its fetcher was broken by the DS UI redesign; removed the same day after the rebuilt Alpine activation chain was validated live in run 30178412079.)
_comment_soft_escalate: Hours after which a 'soft' source stops being exempt and hard-fails the run. Quiet for the first day past its threshold (a cookie re-mint is a chore, not an incident); loud after three (nobody is coming — treat it as an outage). Set <= 0 to disable escalation, which is a legitimate choice for a source that may genuinely lapse indefinitely, but it has to be written down to take effect rather than being the accidental default.
_comment_content: contentStaleness answers a DIFFERENT question from 'thresholds' above, and the distinction is the one this file's first comment already names: a stamp proves a FETCH succeeded, not that the vendor published anything. scripts/check_source_health.py measures, read-only over the tracked exports/archive/*.zip evidence lane, how long each source's raw CSV has been byte-identical - whole board and pick rows separately, because a vendor can refresh players weekly while its pick tiers sit frozen. Motivating measurement (C1-U6 follow-up 7, 2026-08-16): idpTradeCalc fetches fresh every 2h and its board changed 6 times in 165 archives, but its PICK rows have not moved since 2026-07-14 - and it is one of only two families that price picks at all. This is an OBSERVABILITY threshold: it decides what gets reported, never what anything is worth, and it never promotes stale data to fresh or suppresses a signal. 14 days is set above the observed whole-board interval of every source we have archive history for, so it reports a market that has stopped moving rather than one that merely moves slowly.
_comment_acknowledged: acknowledgedFetchOutages: an owner-tracked, DATED downgrade of one source's FETCH outage from FAIL to DEGRADED in scripts/watchdog_freshness.py — nothing else. It is not a vendor-publication gap (a stale _last_success stamp is a fetch failure by construction; content staleness belongs to src/sources/freshness.py), and it never touches the live alert engine, the on-site banner or the contract's warnings. Honoured only while: the entry names a tracking 'issue', carries zoned 'acknowledgedAt'/'expiresAt' at most 14 days apart, now is inside that window, AND the board the same run built shows the source casting NO vote (sourceWeighting.sources[key].votingRows == 0, excludedRows >= 1). A stale source that still votes, an expired/malformed entry, or an unbuildable board stays a hard failure with the refusal named. Exact keys only (no vendor prefix). Renewing an entry is an owner decision, never a way to quiet the job. idpShowCombined (2026-10-16): the prod timer (deploy/idpshow_fetch_and_push.sh, which re-stamps on every successful fetch) has committed nothing since 2026-10-07T20:32Z — every 2h before that it did — so the FETCH is down on the box (most likely the hand-minted IDP Show cookie lapsed: both fetches failing makes the script exit before committing, which also leaves last_status.json at its last HEALTHY write). Separately the vendor's Datawrapper chart has not changed since 2026-08-19, so the freshness weighting already QUARANTINES the board and it votes on 0 of the rows it appears on — the outage cannot move a value. Expires 2026-10-23: re-mint the session on the box, or the job goes red again.
